html:
Kurmi Market is a great market in the old city of Kano, northern Nigeria, founded in the 15th century by Muhammad Rumfa, king of Kano. It is still one of the largest traditional markets in West Africa.

Rumfa ruled from about 1463 to 1499 and made Kano a leading city of the Hausa states. He built a palace and walls, brought in Muslim scholars, and set up the market to draw merchants. Kano sat at the southern end of trans-Saharan trade routes and near the forest trade to the south. Caravans brought salt, horses and North African goods; Kano sold indigo-dyed cloth, leather goods, kola nuts and enslaved people.

The market kept its place under the Sokoto Caliphate in the 19th century, when travellers described Kano as the great trading city of the central Sudan, and under British rule. Its lanes are still known for cloth, dyes, leather and brass.
